reports.title: Harrow Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

lines: •Reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $350 million to $365 million; updated full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to more than $40 million, including fourth quarter Adjusted EBITDA of more than $33 million, compared with prior Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $80 million to $100 million
Achieving our full-year revenue guidance of $350 million to $365 million will require strong execution, but we continue to believe it is achievable.”
We expect more than $33 million in fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, bringing our full-year outlook to more than $40 million.
Today, we are reaffirming our full-year revenue guidance of $350–365 million.
We are lowering our Adjusted EBITDA outlook from $80 million to $100 million to a floor of "more than $40 million," including more than $33 million in the fourth quarter.

desk.headline: Record revenue up 39% to $99.3m, slight beat; full-year revenue range kept but adjusted EBITDA outlook cut to over $40m from $80–100m
results: Revenue hit a third-quarter record of $99.3m, up 39% y/y and 41% on the second quarter; branded products were 84% of sales.
Dry-eye drug VEVYE had a record $39.7m quarter (+75%) and TRIESENCE a record $10.7m; compounding revenue fell 21%.
Net income was $9.8m ($0.25 a share), helped by a $5.0m litigation settlement gain; gross margin held at 75%.
R&D rose to $10.3m from $3.3m and SG&A to $53.1m from $35.9m, so adjusted EBITDA slipped to $21.2m from $22.8m.
Cash was $75.3m at 30 September; the TYRVAYA nasal spray acquisition closed on 1 October.

guidance.summary: Harrow kept its 2026 revenue range of $350–365m but cut adjusted EBITDA guidance to more than $40m from $80–100m, which it calls a floor. It expects more than $33m of adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter.

points: CEO Mark Baum admitted a first-half miss, mainly because VEVYE pricing after discounts and rebates was weaker than assumed; rule changes are now lifting revenue per prescription.
Hitting the revenue range needs Q4 sales of about $136–151m (up 37–52% on Q3); he said finishing modestly below the low end is possible.
The EBITDA cut reflects the first-half shortfall, faster R&D, pulling the G-MELT drug application fee into 2026, TYRVAYA integration costs and higher royalties.
A national health plan covering 10m+ commercial lives will cover VEVYE from January 2027; the BYOOVIZ launch reached more accounts but smaller orders than planned.
From 2027 Harrow plans to return to annual "greater than X" style revenue guidance.

watch: Whether Q4 revenue reaches the $136–151m needed for the full-year range.
The G-MELT drug application, promised before year-end.
VEVYE revenue per prescription and new 2027 guidance with full-year results.
